analysis.title: Druckenmiller's Short, CTAs Are Dumping, Only The Copper Users Are Buying: Who Blinks First?
key_insights: LME copper fell for a fifth straight session on Wednesday (Nov 18, 2026) to $12,770/t, a seven-month low. Comex fell 3.8% to $5.76/lb, per Reuters. Goldman's $15,600/t Dec 2027 LME target is about 22% above spot.

Goldman's Robert Quinn attributes the copper decline to tighter financial conditions plus data center weakness, not to physical fundamentals. These triggered a momentum flip and more bearish speculative flows.

CFTC data for Nov 3-10 showed the 7th straight week of speculative selling in Comex copper. Managed Money, Other and Non-Reportable traders sold another $1.3B, bringing the running total since Sept 22 to $10.8B. The 'Other' category drove it through a sizeable uptick in shorts.
Spec net length fell from a peak of roughly $17.5B in September to about $5B (approximate, read off the chart), the fastest liquidation in the two years shown, and this predates the Nov 18 selloff.

Producers, processors, merchants and users (PMPU) bought $1.1B net, half of it new gross longs. Their gross longs as a share of open interest reached a new multiyear max, about 20%, the highest since the 2022 spike (approximate, read off the chart).

During Nov 10-17 copper lost 4.1% as Goldman's US Financial Conditions Index tightened after inflation data and Fed speak, and data center stocks slipped 3.2%. Managed Money gross longs and the inverted FCI have moved almost in lockstep all year.

Goldman's Shenzhen futures desk said commodities were pricing a hawkish Fed and recovering Middle East supply rather than Chinese demand. Its flow was '4x skewed to sell in base metals'. Shanghai copper fell 3.08%.
Stan Druckenmiller said at the TomorrowX Summit on Tuesday that he is short copper and neutral stocks. Industrial metals then saw a wave of selling, with tin down as much as 8.2%, per Bloomberg.
Copper's medium-term momentum signal turned negative, joining the short-term signal that broke below zero earlier in November. Only the long-term trend is still positive and it is dropping fast.

Goldman's one-week CTA scenario shows roughly $9B of selling (approximate, read off the chart), more than double the largest one-week sell estimate of the past year. Reuters reported computer-driven funds sold on Wednesday after a slide through key support.

Copper's 1-year normalized 25-delta put-call skew hit a 99th percentile 1-year rank, so the usual call premium has largely disappeared. Quinn says the option surface revealed impairment to long-term sentiment. The last comparable skew collapse was in May, before the spring rally faded.

Physical tightness persists. China's import premium for copper hit a record $360/t on Wednesday, up from a $200 record three weeks earlier. Goldman's James McGeoch says Shanghai is short, with more open interest than metal to deliver against it.
Goldman's China materials team said volatility in metal prices, including the physical premium, led to a pushback in end-user order books for the first time in months.
Goldman's recommended trade is long Dec27 copper vs short Dec27 aluminium. The aluminium leg has worked, with LME aluminium at its lowest in almost a year, while the copper leg is losing.

Refined cathode still enters the US duty-free under Section 232. The July 2025 proclamation left a phased tariff on refined copper on the table: 15% from 2027 and 30% from 2028. This pending decision drives US warehouse stockpiling and the record PMPU longs.

Quinn warns that commercial buyer patience is not unlimited. The same category could not withstand a geopolitical reversal in Brent oil in recent weeks. In copper, PMPU is the only bid of size left and its trigger is a tariff headline.

The ZeroHedge author's view is that Goldman's structural case is probably right on a two-year view but that on a two-month view the Fed dominates fundamentals. The author cites a possible December hike, a dollar near a 19-month high and CTA selling not yet finished.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's structural view on a two-year horizon is bullish on tight ex-US stocks and record China premiums, with a $15,600/t Dec 2027 LME target. Near-term flows and financial conditions are negative.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Seven-month low after a fifth straight daily decline.
Down 3.8% on the day, per Reuters.
About 22% above the Nov 18 spot level. Goldman attributes the November selloff to sentiment and Mideast risk, not physical fundamentals.
New record, up from $200 about three weeks earlier, indicating tight physical supply in China.

trade_ideas.description: Long Dec27 LME copper vs short Dec27 LME aluminium
trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman's commodity team expects tight ex-US stocks and US tariff ambiguity to support copper relative to aluminium.
trade_ideas.risk: Near-term financial conditions tightening, CTA selling and a US decision against the refined copper tariff phase-in.

risk_factors: Further tightening of financial conditions, including a possible December Fed hike and a dollar near a 19-month high.
US decision not to proceed with the refined copper tariff phase-in, which would remove the US stockpiling bid.
PMPU capitulation, as happened in Brent oil.
End-user order book pushback from high prices and volatility.
Weakness in data center and AI-related equities.

geopolitical: Near-term Mideast escalation risk and recovering Middle East supply are cited as drivers of the November energy and copper selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's structural case rests on tight ex-US stocks, record China import premiums of $360/t, US tariff ambiguity drawing metal into US stockpiles, and AI and grid demand. Its target is $15,600/t by December 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions, a possible December Fed hike, CTA selling of about $9B (approximate, read off the chart), a 99th percentile put skew and end-user order pushback point lower near term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US signal that the refined copper tariff phase-in will not proceed, which would remove the US stockpiling bid, or PMPU capitulation.

theme_stances.key_argument: Speculative and CTA selling is driven by tighter financial conditions, and the physical industry is the only remaining large buyer.
theme_stances.evidence: the hot money is gone, the machines are next
